subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should Docker-backed `sessions_spawn` startup failures remain accepted-then-async with a typed terminal startup failure, or should sandbox startup be preflighted before returning accepted?
rationale: Both designs can address the silent hang, but the choice changes the public async spawn contract, registry/session state semantics, gateway wait behavior, and the overlap with the broader startup lifecycle tracker.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed logged terminal state that `sessions_history`, `subagents list`, and waits can show for Docker startup failures.

options.title: Preflight sandbox before accept
options.body: Move enough Docker startup validation before the accepted response and reject immediately, accepting added latency and compatibility risk.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle tracker
options.body: Keep this issue as the sandbox-specific proof case while deciding the broader startup lifecycle direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed logged terminal state that `sessions_history`, `subagents list`, and waits can show for Docker startup failures.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history signal across the current subagent spawn, sandbox runtime, and gateway dispatch contract involved in the decision.
